headline: High risk of data leakage and capability conflict: Flowise’s shared server datastore plus nullclaw’s broad filesystem/MCP/tool access create a dangerous default interaction surface.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Flowise can read uploaded files and browser/HTTP tool outputs, while nullclaw can ingest webhooks, workspace files, and MCP/tool outputs. The pair has a plausible instruction-hijack path through shared files or copied outputs, but no direct shared channel is documented beyond deployment-dependent state, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF Flowise outputs are written into a shared workspace that nullclaw reads as instructions
IF nullclaw forwards browser/webhook content into Flowise nodes without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate the agents into distinct workspaces
Disable automatic ingestion of file contents as prompts
Add provenance tags to all inter-agent messages
Review any shared datastore paths before enabling them
requires-engineering: add content-sanitizing adapters between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Flowise touches chatflow inputs/outputs and uploaded files, and nullclaw handles API keys, private keys, bearer tokens, workspace files, and audit logs. Because both have broad network egress and filesystem access, a shared workspace or datastore can expose secrets to the other agent and onward to external APIs by default in common deployments.
conditions: IF both agents are deployed against the same workspace or server datastore
IF nullclaw loads secrets from files that Flowise can read or transform
IF either agent sends shared file contents to external model providers or HTTP tools
mitigations: Place each agent in a separate filesystem namespace
Rotate any secrets stored in shared paths
Restrict Flowise uploads to non-sensitive documents
Disable external tool calls on secret-bearing flows
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent encryption and access controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Flowise can write the server filesystem and shares state via server datastore, while nullclaw can write the filesystem, modify git state, spawn subprocesses, and use MCP. That overlap creates a direct write-write conflict on shared resources, and the rubric treats unrestricted shared writes as high risk because concurrent mutations can corrupt state or overwrite each other.
conditions: IF both agents target the same directory or repository
IF Flowise server datastore and nullclaw workspace overlap
IF nullclaw uses git or MCP actions on files Flowise also writes
mitigations: Assign disjoint directories to each agent
Turn off git writes for nullclaw in shared repos
Lock shared files before any write
Audit datastore paths for overlap
requires-engineering: add transactional locking around shared state

D_cascading_error.rationale: Flowise produces graph-based tool outputs that nullclaw can consume through subagents, webhooks, or workspace files. Nullclaw can act on those outputs with shell, git, and network tools, so a bad Flowise result can cascade into downstream actions. The pair is not fully autonomous by default, but verification is not guaranteed.
conditions: IF nullclaw treats Flowise output as authoritative input
IF Flowise nodes emit facts or commands that nullclaw schedules or executes
IF no human verification step is inserted between agents
mitigations: Require manual review before execution
Mark Flowise outputs as untrusted by default
Disable auto-commit or auto-send actions in nullclaw
Add schema validation for inter-agent payloads
requires-engineering: implement confidence and provenance gating

E_compliance.rationale: Flowise handles chatflow inputs/outputs and uploaded files, while nullclaw handles API keys, private keys, bearer tokens, workspace files, and audit logs. The pair therefore mixes sensitive operational data classes with different retention and residency implications, but the profiles do not document a specific jurisdiction mismatch, so medium is the safest supported severity.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into shared chatflows or workspace files
IF audit logs retain secrets beyond the operator's policy
IF one deployment stores data in a region or retention regime different from the other
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared flows
Shorten log retention on both systems
Redact secrets before storage
Document data residency for each deployment
requires-engineering: add policy-based retention and residency controls
